<security_assessment>
<decision>SAFE</decision>
<details>
The PKGBUILD's top-level scope contains only static variable assignments (`_pkgname`, `pkgname`, `pkgver`, `pkgrel`, `pkgdesc`, `arch`, `url`, `license`, `depends`, `optdepends`, `provides`, `conflicts`, `replaces`, `install`, `changelog`, `options`, `source`, `noextract`, `sha256sums`). There are no command substitutions, no `eval`, no encoded/obfuscated blobs, and no network or file operations executed at source time. Sourcing this file for `makepkg --printsrcinfo` would only parse these definitions.

The `prepare()` and `package()` functions do contain operations (extracting a tarball with `bsdtar` and installing files into `$pkgdir`), but per the scope of this gate those functions are not executed by `--printsrcinfo` and will be reviewed in the full audit. The sources point to the project's own upstream GitHub release and LICENSE, and the checksums are pinned (not SKIP), which is fine. No dangerous top-level behavior is present.
</details>
<evidence>
</evidence>
<summary>Only static variable definitions at top level; no executable malicious code on source.</summary>
</security_assessment>
